text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Public prosecutor's office to investigate the use of staff options schemes at bourse-listed companies. (p1)
- Agreement on shorter working week at Akzo Nobel within reach. (p1)
- Chances of a restart for bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker dashed as Stork pulls out of rescue talks. (p1)
- Shipping group P&O Nedlloyd could lift net earnings by $ 100 million due to planned rate hikes on its Europe- Far East shipping route. (p3)
- Staal Bankiers, a unit of financial services group Achmea, saw 1996 net rise 64 pct to 18.2 million guilders. (p3)
- Belgian icecream maker Artic opens attack on Unilever's icecream market. (p5)
- Builder Kondor Wessels sells its electronics unit S.P.A. Superior Print Assembly. (p5)
- Shares in biotechnology firm Mogen more than halved in value to 15 guilders after news of a takeover bid of 12.50 guilders per share. (p11)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Second case of mad cow disease in the Netherlands discovered on a farm in northern Friesland province. (p1)
- PTT Telecom will offer subscribers three different tariffs linked to number of calls and time of day. (p2)
- Number of passengers travelling with KLM rose 11 percent in the 1996/97 book year, while the load factor rose 1.5 percent to 75.9 percent. (p2)
- Publisher Reed Elsevier has warchest of six billion guilders and is seeking major acquisition. (p17)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Finance ministry seeks to intervene to reduce rapidly rising local authorities taxes. (p1)
- Amsterdam police and public prosecutor furious at continued British allegations of so-called snuff-movies being produced in Amsterdam. (p1)
- Economic affairs minister Hans Wijers plans tougher measures to crack down on imitation branded products. (p7)
- Shipbuilding and engineering group IHC Caland is forecasting earnings growth of 18 percent to 110 million guilders in 1997. (p27)
TROUW
- Dutch banks, except ABN Amro, refuse pyramid scheme organisors as customers. (p4)
- Publisher Wolters Kluwer seeks to form alliances with rival publishers in the field of electronic publishing.
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Westland/Utrecht Hypotheekbank, a subsidiary of financial services group ING, books 15 pct higher 1996 net at 79.1 million guilders (p11)
